minutes.headline: Task force voted to pull the stormwater utility bylaw from the May town meeting warrant, deferring to the override vote
minutes.summary: The Stormwater Task Force voted to withdraw its stormwater utility bylaw article from the May 2026 annual town meeting warrant, agreeing the topic would distract from the town's pending Proposition 2.5 override votes and that public education on the utility had been too limited (worsened by a snowed-out information session). Members also discussed and set aside a possible separate override article to fully fund MS4 stormwater compliance, and a resident pressed the task force on the equity of a commercial-versus-residential fee split before any future utility push, which the task force agreed to investigate further with the assessor's office and local business owners. The task force set its next meeting for April 16.

what_happened.line: Task force voted 5-0 to pull the stormwater utility bylaw from the May town meeting warrant.
Members agreed the bylaw would compete for attention with the town's pending override votes and that public education on it had been too limited.
No consensus formed to put a separate override article on the warrant to fully fund MS4 stormwater compliance instead.
A resident pressed the task force on whether a future utility fee would split fairly between commercial and residential properties, citing the town's single tax rate policy.
The task force agreed to look further into the commercial/residential split with the assessor's office and local business owners before any future utility push.

why_it_matters: The stormwater utility bylaw, which would have created a separate fee to fund MS4 permit compliance, will not appear on the May town meeting warrant this year.

MS4 stormwater compliance funding was reduced in the town manager's override budget proposal at a recent select board workshop, leaving the item bundled into the override question rather than funded separately.

Any future stormwater utility proposal would set fees by property type, including commercial properties, and the task force has committed to studying that split with the assessor's office before proceeding.
